title: Defect-cavity narrowband filter with fixed outer Bragg mirrors and optimized central cavity
scientific_hypothesis: A 29-layer Ta2O5/SiO2 stack with outer Bragg mirror layers fixed at quarter-wave optical thickness and only the central 11 layers optimized will achieve transmittance ≥ 0.95 at 1550 nm while suppressing 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands, with improved convergence stability compared to full-stack optimization.
design_principle: Quarter-wave Bragg mirrors (alternating high/low index layers at λ/4n optical thickness) create high-reflectivity stopbands. Introducing a phase defect or cavity region in the center creates a resonant transmission peak within the stopband. Fixing outer layers reduces the optimization search space dimensionality, preventing extreme thickness compressions and guiding the solver toward stable resonant solutions.
proposed_topology: 29 layers total: Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5/SiO2/Ta2O5, starting with Ta2O5 at air interface, ending with Ta2O5 at substrate interface, with layers 10-20 (11 central layers) as the optimizable cavity region
design_variables: thicknesses of layers 10-20 (11 central cavity layers)
thicknesses of layers 1-9 and 21-29 fixed at quarter-wave values
soft_objectives: maximize mean transmittance in 1550 nm passband
minimize mean transmittance in 1400-1500 nm stopband
minimize mean transmittance in 1600-1700 nm stopband
manufacturing_considerations: quarter-wave outer layers simplify manufacturing control
central cavity thickness tolerance critical for peak wavelength
theory_basis: Quarter-wave Bragg stacks produce stopbands centered at the design wavelength with bandwidth proportional to the index contrast ratio
A central defect layer or cavity region in a Bragg stack creates a narrow transmission resonance within the stopband
Reducing optimization dimensionality by fixing outer mirror layers improves convergence stability in gradient-based thickness optimization
Ta2O5/SiO2 is a standard high-contrast dielectric pair for visible and near-infrared filters
expected_advantages: Faster convergence due to reduced design variable count (11 vs 29 thicknesses)
More stable resonant peak position due to fixed outer mirror phase conditions
Easier manufacturing verification for outer layers at standard quarter-wave thicknesses
Maintained stopband performance from proven Bragg mirror structure
known_risks: Ta2O5 refractive index at 1550 nm recalled as approximately 2.1-2.2 but exact dispersion not verified - would need material dataset lookup
SiO2 refractive index recalled as approximately 1.45 at 1550 nm but exact value not verified
Quarter-wave thickness calculation depends on exact n values - 185 nm for Ta2O5 and 267 nm for SiO2 are approximate based on recalled indices
Fixed outer layers may limit achievable stopband width if quarter-wave assumption is inaccurate for the required 1400-1700 nm suppression range
Central cavity optimization may be sensitive to initial thickness guesses - would benefit from literature on defect-cavity initialization
execution_request_english: Design a 29-layer planar dielectric filter on fused silica substrate with air incidence. Materials are Ta2O5 (Gao) and SiO2 (Lemarchand) in alternating sequence starting with Ta2O5 (Gao) at the air interface. Layers 1-9 and 21-29 (outer Bragg mirrors) have fixed thicknesses: Ta2O5 (Gao) layers at 185 nm, SiO2 (Lemarchand) layers at 267 nm (quarter-wave optical thickness at 1550 nm based on recalled indices). Layers 10-20 (11 central cavity layers) have optimizable thicknesses bounded between 50 nm and 400 nm. Optimize for maximum mean transmittance at 1550 nm (single wavelength target) and minimum mean transmittance across 1400-1500 nm and 1600-1700 nm bands. Use coherent transfer-matrix method solver. Total layer count is exactly 29.
revision_reason: Shift to damping/regional-local search mode anchored around proven high-performance topology from prior iterations. Constrain outer Bragg mirror layers to fixed quarter-wave values based on historical convergence, allocate optimization degrees-of-freedom exclusively to central 11 cavity layers to reduce dimensionality-driven noise and prevent extreme thickness compressions.
